sources.title: Who Needs A Visa
sources.publisher: Embassy of Grenada in the People’s Republic of China, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The page is live on Grenada's Ministry of Foreign Affairs mission domain and directly links the nationality schedule. Its official WordPress metadata shows a 23 December 2023 publication and 24 December 2023 modification, not a 2026 current-force statement.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Updated List of Countries Needing a Visa to visit Grenada

sources.title: Visa Requirements for Traveling to Grenada
sources.publisher: Embassy of Grenada in the People’s Republic of China, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The currently linked Ministry mission PDF identifies itself as updated February 2021. The server object was uploaded in August 2023, but neither its contents nor the current landing page supplies a later operative or effective date.

sources.title: Requirements for Processing Grenada Visa Applications Prior to Arrival
sources.publisher: Embassy of Grenada in the People’s Republic of China, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: This live Ministry mission page was modified on 5 September 2025 according to its official WordPress record. It gives a present-tense entry rule specifically for holders of valid PRC passports, separately from Chinese permanent residents who are not Chinese citizens.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Chinese passport holders do not need a visa for visits to Grenada not exceeding 30 days.

sources.title: Immigration
sources.officialityEvidence: The current central Government of Grenada immigration page provides its visa application form but does not publish a nationality schedule, a current adoption statement for the 2021 schedule, or an exhaustive default.

sources.title: Chapter 145: Immigration Act
sources.publisher: Laws of Grenada, Legal and Legislative Affairs Division
sources.officialityEvidence: Grenada's Legal and Legislative Affairs Division publishes the live Chapter 145 index on laws.gov.gd. The page identifies the Immigration Act and its official document record; the document viewer is currently login-gated.

sources.title: Chapter 145: Immigration Act and subsidiary legislation
sources.officialityEvidence: Grenada Parliament hosts the complete Chapter 145 consolidation, including the Immigration (Visa) Regulations. The live Laws of Grenada portal separately lists the same Chapter 145 record in 2026; neither source publishes a later replacement nationality schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The following persons are exempt from visa requirements on entering the State

policies.title: Valid PRC passport: Grenada short visitor visa-free
policies.summary: Grenada’s current MFA mission guidance expressly exempts citizens of the People’s Republic of China holding valid Chinese passports for visits not exceeding 30 days.
conditions: The rule is limited to a citizen of the People’s Republic of China holding a valid Chinese passport and a visit not exceeding 30 days.
The same current page says a Chinese permanent resident who is not a Chinese citizen must obtain a visa; residence is not generalized into this nationality baseline.
Work, study, residence, cruise-transit, diplomatic, official, service, and other special-document routes are outside this short-visitor ordinary-passport rule.
The online immigration and customs ED form is a pre-arrival declaration, not an ETA or visa.

policies.title: Named foreign nationals: Grenada visa exemption
policies.summary: The Immigration (Visa) Regulations in Grenada’s current Chapter 145 legal record expressly exempt these named nationalities from Grenada visa requirements. These entries add only countries not already covered by the EU–Grenada waiver or the current China-specific MFA guidance.
conditions: The statutory text expressly names citizens of Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, San Marino, Switzerland and the United States as exempt from visa requirements.
Venezuelan citizens are expressly exempt only if they possess valid return or onward tickets.

The legislation concerns visa requirements; it does not guarantee admission, a particular permitted stay, work, study, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, crew, refugee, stateless or other special-document treatment.
The 2021 MFA nationality table is not used to infer treatment of any unlisted nationality because no later operative replacement schedule was recovered.
